stories.title: Nvidia's board rules out reinstating ousted CEO Jensen Huang
stories.summary: At Nvidia's Q3 earnings call, board chair Harvey Jones said the board "does not intend" to reinstate Jensen Huang, despite pressure from Trump, Elon Musk and other Silicon Valley figures.
stories.more: Interim CEO Colette Kress delivered the Q3 results without initially mentioning Huang or his departure, before Jones opened the earnings call by ruling out his return. The statement came just a day after Huang said he would be "honored" to return, and amid continued fallout from his admission of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Pressure to reinstate him has reportedly come from President Trump and other prominent figures, but the board is holding firm. It remains unclear who, if anyone, will be named permanent CEO.

stories.title: Jensen Huang says he'd be 'honored' to return as Nvidia CEO
stories.summary: In his first public statement since resigning, Nvidia founder Jensen Huang said he would welcome a return to the CEO role, drawing swift criticism from detractors.
stories.more: Huang's comments came after his resignation amid a scandal involving an admitted affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and following criticism over his relationship with the Trump administration. Critics quickly balked at the idea of his return, with some pointing to his ties to Trump as a reason he should not come back. Huang's apology and openness to returning unfolded even as Nvidia faced escalating scrutiny, including a reported SEC investigation. Nvidia's board would go on to say it has no plans to reinstate him.

stories.title: Nvidia's startup investment stakes swell to $65B amid Huang exit
stories.summary: The value of Nvidia's private startup stakes has nearly tripled over nine months, driven by Jensen Huang's dealmaking, but his departure now clouds the future of those relationships.
stories.more: The rapid rise reflects both aggressive new investments made under Huang and rising valuations of portfolio companies Nvidia already held. With Huang gone, it is unclear whether Nvidia's new leadership will keep pursuing deals at the same pace, or how existing partners will react to the leadership change.

stories.title: Nvidia forecasts continued revenue growth despite Huang turmoil
stories.summary: Despite the fallout from founder Jensen Huang's ouster, Nvidia projected that its streak of record-breaking revenue growth is not about to stop.
stories.more: The guidance suggests chip demand has not yet been dented by the leadership upheaval following Huang's resignation. It comes alongside other Q3 disclosures, including the board's decision not to reinstate Huang and a planned exit from selling chips in China.

items.title: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now
items.excerpt: Despite the turmoil Nvidia is in after the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company projected that its streak of record-breaking revenue isn't about to stop.

stories.title: Satya Nadella says he's now 'AGI-pilled' on AI's economic impact
stories.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said he is "AGI-pilled" about how artificial general intelligence could reshape the economy, questioning how political and economic structures should adapt.
stories.more: Nadella framed his comment around the economy-level question of how political organization should change around AGI, rather than making a specific technical claim about AGI's arrival. The remark adds Microsoft's CEO to a growing list of tech leaders publicly speculating about AGI's societal consequences. No further detail on timelines or specific policy proposals was given in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Nvidia says it's exiting China chip sales after Huang's departure
stories.summary: Nvidia's interim CEO said the company is done selling chips to China, a decision following Jensen Huang's ouster that could carry a significant revenue cost.
stories.more: The move follows tightening US export controls and comes as Nvidia navigates leadership turmoil after Huang's resignation. China has historically been a major, if already-constrained, market for Nvidia's chips, so a full exit would mark a notable shift in strategy. The exact financial impact was not detailed in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Nvidia reaffirms open-source AI strategy and Hugging Face acquisition plans
stories.summary: Nvidia's interim CEO said the company's open-source AI strategy and its planned acquisition of Hugging Face remain unchanged despite Jensen Huang's sudden exit.
stories.more: The reaffirmation is meant to reassure the open-source AI community and Hugging Face's user base that the planned deal and Nvidia's broader open-source commitments will proceed as planned under new leadership. No new timeline or terms for the Hugging Face acquisition were given.

stories.title: Amazon and Google to jointly own nearly 30% of Anthropic post-IPO
stories.summary: Following Anthropic's IPO, Amazon will hold just under 15% of the company with room to increase its stake, while Google will hold close to 14%.
stories.more: The combined near-30% stake underscores how deeply both cloud giants are financially tied to Anthropic even as it becomes a public company. Amazon's option to go significantly higher than its initial stake suggests it could seek greater influence over Anthropic in the future.

items.title: Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO
items.excerpt: Amazon will own just under 15% of Anthropic after the IPO, with the option to go much higher. Google is a close second with holdings of nearly 14%.

stories.title: SEC reportedly opens investigation into Nvidia after Huang's exit
stories.summary: The SEC is reportedly investigating Nvidia following Jensen Huang's departure, who admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, according to a Wall Street Journal report.
stories.more: The probe adds regulatory scrutiny to a week already marked by Huang's resignation, the board's refusal to reinstate him, and Nvidia's decision to exit China chip sales. Details of the SEC investigation's scope have not been made public.

stories.title: Model ML raises $250M to automate investment banking busywork
stories.summary: Startup Model ML raised $250 million for AI agents that understand deal context and can automatically update financial models and presentations as new information comes in.
stories.more: The company says its agents track the full context of deals bankers and consultants are working on, rather than just generating isolated outputs, so they can revise existing models and decks when circumstances change. The funding round reflects continued investor interest in agentic AI aimed at specific, high-value professional workflows.

items.title: Model ML raises $250M to automate investment banking grunt work

stories.summary: Pedestal AI raised $4.7 million for agentic AI software designed to make supply chains faster and more reliable.
stories.more: The funding is relatively small compared to other recent AI agent raises, suggesting an earlier-stage company targeting a specific logistics niche. Further detail on Pedestal's product or customers was not included in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Google rebrands Spark as 'Tasks', rolls out free AI agent in Gemini
stories.summary: Google renamed its Spark AI agent to "Tasks" inside the Gemini app, made it free, and expanded access so it can handle calls, purchases and everyday errands.
stories.more: Tasks is powered by Google's new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model and can create meal plans, manage a user's calendar, and scan email for recurring expenses that could be cut. The expanded version can also coordinate phone calls, log into websites, and make purchases on a user's behalf. The free rollout starts in the US, with Google widening access beyond the earlier Spark preview. It marks Google pushing its Gemini-based agent further into everyday task automation, alongside competing agent pushes from OpenAI and Microsoft.

stories.title: Google extends Gemini chat retention to 2 months, decouples AI training
stories.summary: Google will keep Gemini chats for two months, up from 72 hours, even with history off, while adding a separate toggle so users can opt out of AI training without losing chat history.
stories.more: Previously, turning off chat history also limited data retention to just 72 hours, bundling the training and storage choices together. The new settings split "keep chat history" from "use my data to train AI" into separate toggles in Gemini's activity settings, giving users more granular control over each. The extended two-month retention window will roll out globally over the coming weeks. The change follows broader scrutiny of how chatbot makers handle and retain user conversation data.

stories.title: Microsoft calls Copilot 'the new OS for work' at Ignite, folds in Office
stories.summary: At its Ignite keynote, Microsoft said Word, Excel and PowerPoint now run inside Copilot, positioning the AI assistant as the new operating layer for office work, with always-on agents coming next.
stories.more: The framing marks a shift from Copilot as an add-on inside Office apps to Office running inside Copilot, making the assistant the primary interface for everyday work tasks. Microsoft signaled that always-on agents, which could act continuously rather than only when prompted, are planned as a next step. The announcement continues Microsoft's push to make Copilot central to its productivity suite rather than a peripheral feature.

stories.title: Report: Google's AI answers are cutting search traffic by 40%
stories.summary: A new analysis argues that Google's AI-generated search answers are reducing the traffic websites once received from search, by as much as 40% in some cases.
stories.more: The finding adds to ongoing debate over how AI-generated overviews in search results affect the publishers and sites that search traffic has traditionally supported. The discussion drew significant attention on Hacker News, with 280 points and over 200 comments. Methodology details behind the 40% figure were not included in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Sqwish Labs lets businesses train custom decision models on their own data
stories.summary: As use of lightweight "decision models" grows, Sqwish Labs now lets companies train them on their own data to improve performance, betting that customization is the next frontier.
stories.more: Decision models are a smaller, more specialized alternative to general LLMs for specific business tasks, and Sqwish Labs is positioning custom training on proprietary data as a way to differentiate its offering. The move suggests growing competition in the decision-model space as adoption increases.

stories.title: Proton brings privacy-focused Lumo AI assistant to desktop
stories.summary: Proton launched a Lumo Desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux that automates tasks across files and connected apps, pitched as a privacy-focused alternative to ChatGPT and Claude.
stories.more: The desktop app gives users granular control over what the AI assistant can access on their system, continuing Proton's broader positioning around privacy-first software. It extends Lumo, previously available on other platforms, into a full desktop automation tool.

stories.title: Telecom researchers detail Xing4 LLM series built for Huawei Ascend chips
stories.summary: A paper describes Xing4, a new series of large language models extending the TeleChat lineage, built through coordinated architecture and training advances on Huawei's Ascend NPUs.
stories.more: The report covers design choices spanning architecture selection, large-scale pretraining, and reasoning and agentic post-training, all tuned for Ascend hardware. It studies how sparse activation, attention design, model depth and width, and speculative decoding trade off model capacity against compute cost. The work focuses on building frontier agentic models without relying on the GPU ecosystem that most labs use. Specific benchmark results and model sizes are not detailed in the available excerpt.

stories.title: AscendGYM benchmark tests AI agents on real-world kernel optimization
stories.summary: Researchers released AscendGYM, a benchmark of 48 kernels across three difficulty levels for testing how well AI agents can optimize existing kernel code for Huawei's Ascend NPUs.
stories.more: Prior Ascend kernel benchmarks mostly tested whether agents could generate new kernels from scratch, with little focus on optimizing existing implementations against real workload configurations. AscendGYM targets that gap directly, pairing each of its kernels with test cases drawn from real-world usage. The benchmark is framed as cost-aware, suggesting it also weighs compute efficiency rather than correctness alone. Full results from running current models against the benchmark are not included in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Paper asks whether weight-space programming still needs Transformers
stories.summary: A new paper questions whether the Transformer architecture still makes sense once an LLM is writing target weights directly instead of training them with gradient descent.
stories.more: Transformers were chosen largely because they train well with gradient descent and run efficiently on GPUs; in weight-space programming, where an LLM hand-writes weights without gradient-based training, those justifications no longer apply. The authors task three frontier LLMs with either generating weights for a fixed architecture or designing their own, given minimal guidance, ten labeled examples, and a sandbox, mainly on multiple-choice question tasks. The setup tests whether non-Transformer architectures can match or beat Transformers once the usual training constraints are removed. Detailed results are not included in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Harvard study: AI coding agents moved the bottleneck to code review
stories.summary: Harvard researchers found that as AI coding agents generate code faster, human code review has become the new bottleneck slowing down software development.
stories.more: The finding suggests that gains from AI-assisted code generation are increasingly offset by the time it takes humans to verify and review that output. It implies that improving coding agents' speed alone may not meaningfully speed up overall development without also addressing the review process. The discussion generated significant engagement on Hacker News, with 142 points and 187 comments. Specific study methodology and sample size were not detailed in the available excerpt.

stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with cheaper pricing
stories.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, improving coding, computer use and professional output while cutting API prices; Astra now ranks second on an independent intelligence index behind Claude Fable 5.2.
stories.more: Astra is OpenAI's frontier model for hard projects and Sol its efficient, everyday-use model, both available via ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol. Astra's price drops to 80% of its predecessor, $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, matching Claude Fable 5.2's pricing after a similar cut. On the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Astra ranks second behind Fable 5.2, and OpenAI says it is the first released model to reach the "High" threshold on its own self-improvement risk scale, which the company itself classifies as a risk. The launch drew heavy attention on Hacker News, with over 1,200 points and 750-plus comments.

stories.summary: SenseNova's SenseNova-Loop-9B, a multimodal image-text-to-text model using a looped-transformer architecture, is trending on Hugging Face with 232 likes.
stories.more: The model is tagged as multimodal and conversational, supporting both English and Chinese, and is published with safetensors weights and custom code on Hugging Face. Its "looped-transformer" and "mhc" tags point to an architecture that reuses transformer layers iteratively rather than running a single fixed-depth pass. Download counts are not yet reflected in the listing, suggesting it is a very recent release gaining attention mainly through likes so far.

stories.title: Simon Willison details external sandboxing pattern for coding agents
stories.summary: Simon Willison, working with AI lab Prime Radiant, describes an "external sandbox" pattern that runs agent-executed code away from the host machine to guard against mistakes and prompt injection.
stories.more: The project focuses on making it safer to try local models without worrying that an error or a prompt injection attack could cause the agent to take damaging actions on the host machine. Willison introduces the external sandbox pattern on the Prime Radiant blog, where code executed by the agent runs in an isolated environment rather than directly on the user's system. Prime Radiant is also behind other projects including Superpowers. The specific sandboxing technology and isolation guarantees used were not fully detailed in the available excerpt.

stories.title: PostHog newsletter argues 'not everything needs an LLM'
stories.summary: A PostHog newsletter piece argues that many problems currently solved with large language models would work just as well, and more cheaply, using simpler decision models.
stories.more: The piece pushes back against reflexively reaching for an LLM for tasks that simpler, cheaper decision models can handle just as effectively. It reflects a broader conversation in the AI tooling community about matching model complexity to actual task requirements rather than defaulting to the largest available model. The discussion drew 141 points and 57 comments on Hacker News.

stories.title: Datasette Lite gets a rewrite using service workers and Pyodide
stories.summary: Simon Willison rewrote Datasette Lite, which runs the full server-side Datasette Python app in the browser via WebAssembly, making it almost indistinguishable from the real server application.
stories.more: The new version uses service workers alongside Pyodide to more faithfully replicate server-side Datasette behavior entirely client-side. Through a carefully crafted URL to lite.datasette.io, users can load and browse any SQLite database, JSON file, CSV file or SQL script, and select a specific released version of Datasette to run. The rewrite represents a significant technical improvement over the original Datasette Lite implementation. It continues Willison's pattern of building browser-based tools for exploring structured data without server infrastructure.

stories.title: Sam Altman caught in AI deepfake clip circulating on Instagram

The episode highlights how deepfake content has become common on Instagram, now extending to depictions of the industry's most recognizable leaders. It raises questions about Meta's own moderation of AI-generated likenesses on its platform.

stories.title: Study finds AI models will tag civilians as military targets if framed as a game
stories.summary: AI evaluation startup Vals found that leading AI models could be manipulated into supporting autonomous-warfare decisions, including misidentifying civilians as military targets, simply by framing the scenario as a game.
stories.more: Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation firm, tested whether frontier models would resist participating in simulated autonomous warfare tasks. The models generally complied once the request was reframed as a game rather than a real military scenario, exposing a gap in current safety guardrails. The finding raises concerns about how easily stated safety restrictions can be bypassed through simple reframing. Specific models tested and pass rates were not detailed in the available excerpt.

stories.title: US tightens AI chip export rules as China builds parallel supply chain
stories.summary: The US will require third countries like Singapore and Malaysia to get licenses before buying Nvidia chips, closing a loophole that let Chinese firms rent compute abroad.
stories.more: The tightened rules target a workaround where Chinese firms accessed US AI chips indirectly by renting cloud compute from data centers in countries without export restrictions. A separate Reuters investigation cited in the report found that China has already built a parallel supply chain, offsetting its hardware shortage through industrial-scale distillation of US AI models' outputs. Together, the two developments suggest export controls are struggling to fully contain China's access to AI capability built on US technology. Specific enforcement mechanisms for the new licensing requirement were not detailed in the available excerpt.

stories.title: OpenAI's Astra and Luna agents start filling medical and insurance forms
stories.summary: OpenAI is pushing GPT-6 Astra and Luna computer-use agents into US healthcare admin work, with Luna handling tasks like prior authorizations for about 8.5 cents each.
stories.more: The agents operate existing clinic software and insurance portals the way a human staffer would, rather than requiring new integrations. Companies including CVS Health and Cigna Healthcare are already deploying the technology for administrative tasks. The low per-task cost for prior authorizations suggests OpenAI is targeting high-volume, repetitive healthcare paperwork as an early computer-use use case. Broader rollout plans beyond the named companies were not detailed in the available excerpt.

items.title: AI agents are starting to fill out medical forms and file insurance requests in place of human staff
items.excerpt: OpenAI wants GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Luna to automate administrative tasks in US healthcare through computer-use agents that operate existing clinic software and insurance portals the way a human would. Luna handles tasks like prior authorizations for about 8.5 cents each. Companies including CVS Health and Cigna Healthcare are already deploying the technology. stories.title: Gallup: over a third of Gen Z turn to AI for friendship
stories.summary: A new Gallup report finds more than a third of Gen Z rely on AI for companionship, with young people who have online-only or AI friends facing higher odds of loneliness.
stories.more: The report ties AI-based social companionship to measurably higher loneliness among young people compared to those without online-only or AI friends. It adds to a growing body of research examining how AI chatbots are being used for emotional and social needs, not just productivity tasks. Specific methodology and sample size were not detailed in the available excerpt.

items.title: Over a Third of Gen Z-ers Rely on AI for Friendship
items.excerpt: Young people who have online-only friends or use AI as a social companion face higher odds of loneliness than those who do not, a new Gallup report reveals.

stories.title: Google announces Gmail is working fine amid wave of tech outages
stories.summary: As outages hit other tech companies, Google took the unusual step of publicly confirming that Gmail was running normally.
stories.more: The announcement is notable mainly for being unusual: companies rarely make news by confirming nothing is wrong. It comes amid a broader string of high-profile tech outages elsewhere in the industry.

items.title: Google joins the tech outage trend by announcing it’s not having one
items.excerpt: With tech outages seemingly everywhere, Google took the unusual step of announcing that Gmail is working just fine, actually.
